paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Edinburgh, including the City of Edinburgh Council's own service, Foster with Edinburgh, and independent agencies working across Scotland. The council's fostering team gives information and advice on becoming a carer, runs a training calendar and support groups for its carers, and holds drop-in sessions online and in person for people weighing it up.

Edinburgh changed how it pays its own foster carers for 2026-27. In May 2026 it announced a move to a single fee that no longer depends on the age of the child, rising to £307.50 a week; the council said this was an increase of around 60% for people caring for children under 12. Specialist fees, including for caring for a disabled child, rise to £490.06 a week, and continuing care fees to £307.50 a week. The age-related Scottish Recommended Allowance, which covers the child's day-to-day costs, went up by 3.8%.

Putting fee and allowance together, the council says its carers can receive between £485.20 and £696.78 a week to foster one child under 16, depending on the type of placement and the child's age and needs. That is between £25,230.40 and £36,232.56 a year. The council said it wants fostering to be financially sustainable for carers.

Before you choose, speak to the council and two or three of the services above about the children they most need homes for, the training and the support out of hours. If you live outside the city, see the Fife and Scotland pages too.
